transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I'm... I'm not really sure why I have to be here. My manager at the restaurant told me I needed to come. I guess... well, they got scared at work. I was just... freezing up, I guess. During service. Or doing things wrong. Like, I'd just be standing by the soda machine with the key for the cash drawer... and I'd just be saying table numbers over and over, instead of actually closing out the checks. I don't really know why.
During those moments when you were frozen and repeating the table numbers, were you aware of what was happening around you, and do you remember it afterward?
Um... I don't really know. It's... mostly just a blur. I guess I don't really remember it happening. Not clearly, anyway. I'm not sure.
During these episodes, did anyone notice you having any jerking or shaking movements, biting your tongue, or losing control of your bladder or bowels?
No... no, nobody said anything about that. Just... just the freezing up. That's all.
When these episodes happen, about how long do they typically last—seconds, a couple of minutes, or longer?
I don't really know. Nobody told me how long it lasted. Maybe a few minutes? I'm just not sure.
After one of these episodes ends, do you feel confused, drowsy, or unusually tired afterward, or do you feel back to normal right away?
Um... I don't think so. I guess I just... go back to normal. I don't really remember feeling tired or anything like that. I just go back to what I was doing.
Do these episodes tend to happen during particularly stressful, busy, or emotionally upsetting moments at work, or can they occur at any random time regardless of what's going on?
I don't know. Just... any time, I guess. I haven't really noticed a pattern.
Have you experienced any particularly stressful, traumatic, or overwhelming events—either recently or in the past—that seemed to start around the same time these episodes began?

Um... I don't know about traumatic. But... I guess this whole change has been building for a while. About a year and two months, maybe. That's... that's when they asked me to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities at work. I guess it started around then.
During one of these episodes, if a coworker called your name loudly or touched your arm, do you think that would snap you out of it, or would you remain unresponsive regardless?
Um... I'm not really sure. I don't think anyone has ever tried to do that. They mostly just... leave me alone, I guess.
Have these episodes ever happened on your days off or outside of work, or have they only occurred while you were at the restaurant?

Um... I guess mostly at work. That's... that's where people noticed it. It scared them, I think. Because I'd just... freeze up. Right in the middle of a rush. Or I'd do things wrong... like, I'd stand by the soda machine with the key for the cash drawer, just... saying table numbers out loud instead of actually closing out the checks. I don't know if it happens at home. I'm usually just by myself.

Have you noticed whether these episodes tend to happen specifically when you're feeling overwhelmed or anxious about your responsibilities as shift lead, or do they seem to occur even during calmer, less stressful moments at work?
Um... I don't really know. I haven't... I haven't really noticed a pattern with it. It just sort of happens. I don't think I'm really paying attention to how busy it is when it does.

Right before one of these episodes starts, do you ever notice any warning signs—like a strange smell, a rising feeling in your stomach, dizziness, or a sense of déjà vu—or does it just happen suddenly without any warning?
Um... no. I don't think so. I haven't... I haven't noticed any strange smells or anything like that. It just... it just happens, I guess.

Have you ever been able to stop or shorten one of these episodes yourself—like by trying to focus, calming down, or forcing yourself to snap out of it—or once it starts, does it always run its course no matter what you do?
Um... I don't think I can stop them. I just... I don't really know what's happening until it's over, or until someone says something. So... no, I can't snap out of it.
Have you ever had one of these episodes happen while you were asleep, or has someone noticed unusual movements while you were sleeping?
No... not that I know of. I live alone, so... there's no one around to really notice if I did. I just... I just sleep through the night, mostly.
During these episodes, do people who witness you say your eyes are open and staring, or closed—and if closed, do you resist when someone tries to open your eyelids?

Um... I'm not really sure. Like I said, I live alone, so... nobody's really around to see. And if it happens at work... no one's ever told me what my eyes are doing. They just... they just tell me I spaced out. So, I don't know.

Aside from these specific freezing episodes, do you ever have times—at work or at home—where you feel disconnected from yourself or your surroundings, like you're watching yourself from outside, or where you have gaps in your memory for things you must have done?
No... I don't think so. I mean, I forget things sometimes, like where I put my keys, but... not whole gaps. And I don't... I don't feel like I'm outside myself. Just the freezing things.
Have you ever had a significant head injury, a seizure as a child, or does anyone in your family have epilepsy?
No... nothing like that. I've never hit my head bad or anything. And... no, I didn't have seizures. I don't think anyone in my family has epilepsy, either... at least, nobody's ever told me they do.

When you think back to the times these episodes happened, do they seem to cluster around moments when you're feeling anxious or under pressure about your shift lead duties, or do they really seem to come out of nowhere with no connection to how you're feeling emotionally?
I don't know... I guess they just happen. I haven't really noticed if I'm stressed or anything. They just kind of come out of nowhere, I think.

Have you noticed whether these freezing episodes tend to happen specifically when you're handling money or closing out checks at the register, or do they occur even when you're doing other, unrelated tasks?

I guess... it's mostly when I'm supposed to be doing something specific. Like... well, the other day, I was supposed to be closing checks. But I just... ended up standing by the soda machine. I had the key for the register, but I wasn't using it. I was just standing there... saying table numbers out loud. I wasn't really doing anything else. It... it kind of freaked out the other servers.

During these episodes, have coworkers ever mentioned seeing you make any repetitive movements—like lip-smacking, chewing, fumbling with your hands, or picking at your clothes—besides the freezing and repeating table numbers?
Um... no. They didn't say anything about that. Just... just that I was standing there. Nobody mentioned... chewing or anything. Just the talking.
Have you ever had an EEG or brain imaging done because of these episodes, and if so, do you know what the results showed?
No... I haven't. Nobody ever told me to get anything like that done.
